blocks.text: What it does

This module provides 2D scene and flight rendering using standard HTML5 Canvas 2D contexts. It projects double-precision celestial body positions, orbits, planetary surfaces, day and night lighting, craters, latitude parallels, trajectory lines, ship chevrons and throttle flames to screen coordinates using an independent camera transform. Render quality and pixel ratio caps never modify physical celestial bodies or collision geometry.
Provides and requires

items: Provides render.canvas@1.0.0 through the CANVAS_DRAWING key: a CanvasRendererFactory that creates SceneRenderer instances.
Requires core.motion@^1.0.0 through the CORE_MOTION key: binds surface terrain query ports for procedural elevation sampling.
Fills the render.canvas slot in presentation profiles.

blocks.text: Settings

items: maxPixelRatio (default 1, from 0.5 to 4, step 0.1): Maximum backing pixels per CSS pixel. Lower values reduce raster cost and memory; higher values sharpen high-DPI output. Collision geometry is unchanged.

blocks.text: Lifecycle

items: Initialization binds surface queries from CORE_MOTION, captures maxPixelRatio from settings, registers this guide, and provides CANVAS_DRAWING.
create(canvas, options) instantiates a CanvasRenderer wrapping the canvas 2D context. The factory registers each active renderer for cleanup.
drawScene(frame, timer) and draw(frame, timer) project celestial coordinates, draw procedural backdrops, bodies, orbit rings, overlays, ships and labels.
dispose marks the renderer disposed. Disposing the factory releases all tracked renderer instances.

blocks.text: Remove or replace

Canvas 2D is the default 2D rendering provider for targets without WebGL support. To replace it, implement a presentation module providing render.canvas@1.0.0 in the render.canvas slot. Alternatively, select render.webgl for GPU-accelerated rendering.
Stability

Module version 0.2.0 uses API space-sim-game-api/2 and manifest format space-sim-module/2. Both are pre-freeze: renderer interfaces and scene frame definitions can evolve before API freeze with documented migration paths.
Example

examples/modules/render-canvas demonstrates consuming render.canvas@1.0.0 to create a scene renderer, project celestial frames, and manage renderer disposal. Build and validate it from the repository root:

npm run module:build -- examples/modules/render-canvas/module.json /tmp/example-canvas.spacemod
npm run module:validate -- /tmp/example-canvas.spacemod

VehicleAppearance may declare metresPerUnit and local detail paths. Near-view hull/flame/details scale by the camera pixels per metre; sub-eight-pixel hulls become navigation markers. Match artwork to authoritative contactRadiusMetres; optional geometry never changes collision authority.

Tile chunks: features.tileChunks version 1 qualifies unlit 32x32 foreground tiles, optional rotationRadians about origin, and an optional simple clipPolygon in chunk-local metres before rotation (even-odd fill). Tiles, clip vertices and registered palettes are borrowed immutable data through drawing; dispose releases renderer resources. Check this feature before requesting clipping; absent support requires an explicit vector fallback or compatibility error. This subset does not qualify underground walls, light encoding or dense streaming. Canvas transforms full footprints; WebGL uses one instanced tile draw and one stencil mask draw per clipped chunk. Palette IDs used by the bounded successor profile are 0..4. Module layers validate finite rotation and detached clipping vertices; clip vertices share the existing 4,096-point layer budget with line vertices.

Tile conformance: actual features.tileChunks version 1 declares body-local rotation and simple even-odd clipPolygon. Optional lightEncoding=nibble, paletteEntries=1024, walls=true and buffers=borrowed-through-draw declare the supplied-light profile; requireTileChunkFeatures preflights essential consumers. Primitive lightEncoding=nibble validates 0..1023 IDs and 0..15 light, with brightness 0.2+0.8*n/15 and omitted light full. Omitted encoding retains legacy renderer lighting. Palette registration copies 1..1024 hex entries (#RGB/#RRGGBB/#RRGGBBAA); zero is transparent, missing slots use grey in strict mode and unknown palettes use the registered default. Cosmetic walls show only through air at 55% brightness; no underground light propagation or terrain authority is implied. Chunks draw before vector overlays and labels, outside the v1 shader-pack ABI. Arrays stay caller-owned and unchanged until all draws complete, then may be reused. Re-register palettes on renderer replacement; dispose releases resources. Missing optional tile support uses a declared vector fallback; no hardware-performance claim.

Optional RenderBody.air replaces legacy sky/glow, including mode off. Discover features.independentAir version 1 first. Modes air/clouds request a bounded radial shell; Canvas renders atmosphere/sky only and WebGL also renders decorative clouds, outside the union of canonical body ground masks and before trajectories/pads/hulls/overlay cues. Heights are metres above maximum terrain radius (or body radius); colors/opacity are normalized, phaseRadians is supplied in the body frame. The renderer never advances a clock or changes terrain/contact. Optional air.sunDirection uses the shared system direction without relighting ground. Missing air preserves legacy/Classic rendering. WebGL without stencil omits this optional capability; use an explicit clear/legacy fallback. No shader-pack ABI change, effect target, texture, physical weather or spherical projection is implied. The app controls low-tier cloud removal and pause/warp policy. See independentAirExample in examples/modules/render-canvas/src/main.ts. Near views include an opaque lighting-based sky (day/twilight/night), aligned to the local outward direction. It fades by altitude within heightMetres and by apparent body size for orbital maps. Canonical ground masking still applies; mode off retains the clear-space comparison. Canvas is a deliberately low-detail fallback: cloud requests render atmosphere/sky only. It does not mutate the requested air descriptor, masks, clock or WebGL quality.

Optional features.planetOverview version 1 accepts RenderBody.overview: coarse-to-fine body-fixed polar summaries, premultiplied linear RGBA, <=2048 entries per level and <=12 levels. Providers filter tiny bodies and shade an illustrative sphere inside unchanged canonical terrain/coasts; no new topology or collision. Canvas uses two radial gradient bands (<=1024 triangles); WebGL uses four (<=4096 triangles). Canonical ground remains complete when absent or unsupported, while air and gameplay cues retain their order. No fine chunks, new textures, effect targets or v1 shader ABI changes. Descriptor and arrays stay immutable for their lifetime; replace the descriptor object on palette/content revision. See planetOverviewExample in examples/modules/render-canvas/src/main.ts. Optional overview.surface continues an opaque three-material, 16 m canonical ribbon: <=8192 angular columns, <=8 depth rows, two packed 2-bit identities/leaf byte, <=13 angular-only mips with two coverage bytes/bin (third residual), linear RGB palette. Both providers filter physical footprints before detail readiness, without descriptor calls or fine chunks. Exact accepted palette identities remain at resolved coverage. Canvas may use fewer depth bands within its triangle cap; the complete canonical backing remains on overflow. Immutable arrays are borrowed, never modified by the provider. The optional surface path uses up to seven WebGL radial bands with shared vertex colors and restrained filled relief at existing profile feature anchors; Canvas keeps two broad gradient bands on the original canonical chords. WebGL angular refinement inserts points on canonical chords only, targets up to96 angular segments, simplifying small bodies, and never changes the canonical mask or contact. Physical surface colors stay unlit, matching foreground identities; only the globe face receives sphere/feature lighting and filtered presentation contrast. The successor face diffuses the circumference material mixture inward harmonically, retaining the actual filtered ribbon at the rim; this avoids polar spokes without inventing interior geology. Shared mesh vertices/colors tighten its WebGL surface-path cap to1536 triangles, within the general4096 limit. Source profile features supply filled relief only, never physical displacement. Angular and radial physical footprints are independent; the visible skin does not average unrelated deep bands. A rim-focused view transitions to the actual16m ribbon as it spans2..8px, independently of global body size. Globe-only continuation derives from the actual upper4m, with2.2x filtered display contrast; unlit physical colors and canonical targets remain unchanged.

Fallback quality: Canvas defaults to one backing pixel per CSS pixel, low-quality backdrop without nebula/galaxies, no decorative clouds and two broad planet gradient bands. Explicit creator maxPixelRatio overrides remain supported. Flight controls, canonical terrain/contact, selected circumference targets and local material data remain supported. WebGL quality/preferences are independent and unchanged.

Near-view summary agreement: WebGL inserts body-fixed atlas-aligned columns (~1.5m minimum spacing) within32m either side of the view centre, on the existing canonical chords. A visible-segment budget limits the physical skin to1280 triangles inside the1536 total atlas cap, adapting depth rows. Shared columns/colors keep storage bounded. Both providers filter actual angular mesh support independently from radial depth; Canvas keeps its coarse two-band fallback. No fine cells/chunks, new terrain authority or shader ABI are introduced. Outside the selected region and at finite atlas leaf support, mixtures remain approximate until fine detail is ready.
